text: What Is a Dwarf Planet? Meaning and the 2026 ED138 Discovery?. A dwarf planet is a small, round object that orbits the sun directly but has not cleared its neighborhood of other objects of similar size. Astronomers call the newest candidate 2026 ED138, a possible dwarf planet about 4.3 billion miles from the sun.. Astronomers announced a possible new dwarf planet beyond Neptune, called 2026 ED138, after the Vera C. Rubin Observatory detected it in data collected earlier this year. The announcement came at a planetary sciences meeting in Spokane, Washington, in late October 2026.. To qualify, an object must orbit the sun, be massive enough that its own gravity pulls it into a rounded shape, and fail to dominate its orbital path. The International Astronomical Union set these rules in 2006, when Pluto was reclassified. The IAU recognizes five confirmed dwarf planets: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake. Ceres is the only one found between Mars and Jupiter, in the asteroid belt. Eris lies at the outer edge of the solar system, and Pluto, Haumea and Makemake sit in the Kuiper Belt, an icy ring beyond Neptune. The candidate 2026 ED138 was found in Vera C. Rubin Observatory data and could measure up to 930 miles across, according to scientists. Its size and shape still need confirmation from other telescopes. Rubin is expected to find about 32,000 more objects beyond Neptune over the next decade, and several of them may be dwarf planets. Researchers say the find shows the observatory is working as planned.
